subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Integrated Circuits: A Factory on a Chip
description: A 60-second lesson on Integrated Circuits: A Factory on a Chip.

hook.text: An integrated circuit packs millions of components onto a chip smaller than your fingernail.

buildup.text: Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce independently invented the IC in 1958-59. Kilby used germanium; Noyce used silicon.

discovery.text: Photolithography prints circuit patterns with UV light on silicon wafers. Each layer adds transistors, resistors, and wires.

twist.text: A modern chip factory costs $20 billion. Only three companies on Earth can build leading-edge chips.

climax.text: TSMC in Taiwan manufactures chips for Apple, AMD, and Nvidia. A single disruption could halt the global tech industry.

punchline.text: Print circuits with light. Shrink them every year. Run the world.

quiz.question: Why are modern chip factories so expensive to build?
options: They require rare raw materials imported from only one country
Photolithography at nanometer scales demands extremely precise and costly equipment
Government regulations require extensive safety certifications
